title: Fin-focused extension of the flying-fish blueprint: the zebrafish pectoral fin and its parts, with proxy-fish gene links re-attached to the structure each record names
constraint: Every node below the pectoral fin is a zebrafish anatomy (ZFA) term, and every gene link is a zebrafish or medaka record. None of it is a flying-fish measurement. Note what that does and does not mean: an annotated draft genome of a flying fish exists (Hirundichthys speculiger, 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes; see map.vetted.json flying_fish_genome), so the gap is not missing genes but missing expression and phenotype records, which exist only for zebrafish and medaka. A flying fish's wing is an enlarged pectoral fin.
causation_warning: 'expressed in' is detection, not causation. 'required for' is a loss-of-function phenotype at exactly the structure ZFIN names, never pushed down to parts or cells. 'sufficient for' is a verified gain-of-function allele that changes the structure's size, not one that makes it.

propagation_rules.expressed in: not propagated in this file (each link sits on the structure the record names)
propagation_rules.required for: never propagates down; not propagated up in this file either

queries.zfa_closure: ZFIN anatomy_relationship.txt rows with relationship 'part of', closed transitively from ZFA:0001161 'pectoral fin' and from the 'pectoral fin bud' term; develops_from rows between terms of that set kept as precursor edges

blueprint_join.note: The organ node of this file is the blueprint's pectoral fin; everything below it is new and zebrafish-defined. 'mesenchyme pectoral fin' (ZFA:0001000) is the blueprint's one fin tissue.

wing_genes._honest_summary: All three wing genes' ZFIN evidence sits at the ORGAN level or above: kcnk5b at 'pectoral fin' (gain-of-function alleles, heterozygous rows, adult) and at generic 'fin', 'lepidotrichium' and 'caudal fin actinotrichium' terms that are not pectoral-specific; slc43a2a at 'pectoral fin' (one adult RT-PCR expression row and heterozygous dmh26 phenotype rows, which fail the homozygosity rule, from the Daane paper) with homozygous rows on the caudal fin; kcnh2a only as RT-PCR expression in generic 'fin' and 'regenerating fin', no phenotype row in any single-gene fish. No row for any of the three names a fin tissue or a cell type. 'Required for' is never pushed down.
